issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a public Farm.singFarmSong() method (to print the Old MacDonald song for all animals), but the solution implementation provides a public method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch between the intended API (singFarmSong) and the solution (playFarmSong) is structural and can confuse students about which method to implement or call, and may cause automated tests or graders expecting singFarmSong() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification and template by renaming the solution's public playFarmSong() method to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to playFarmSong(). Ensure the public API matches the method name used in the problem statement and template so students and automated tests have a consistent expectation.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a method named singFarmSong() on Farm, but the solution implementation provides a method named playFarmSong() instead. This mismatch breaks the direct one-to-one mapping students expect (and leaves calls in Main referencing singFarmSong()), creating confusion about the correct method name to implement and call.
